messages.subject: RS-DBI over SSL?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
   I have been using RPostgreSQL for a while. Our company made some changes 
to the DB today and said we must have SSL enabled now in our configuration 
to connect. I don't have a problem connecting to the PostgreSQL command 
line (with "psql") but can't make a connection from R. Is there a way in 
RS-DBI to make the connection using SSL, like the way we can add a 
"?ssl=true" parameter in RJDBC? I ran this by Dirk and he suggested I post 
it here.

   Thanks

messages.subject: Re: RS-DBI over SSL?
messages.body_plain:
On 10/04/2012 12:03 PM, Bibudh Lahiri wrote:
> 
>    Hi,
>    I have been using RPostgreSQL for a while. Our company made some
> changes to the DB today and said we must have SSL enabled now in our
> configuration to connect. I don't have a problem connecting to the
> PostgreSQL command line (with "psql") but can't make a connection from
> R. Is there a way in RS-DBI to make the connection using SSL, like the
> way we can add a "?ssl=true" parameter in RJDBC? I ran this by Dirk and
> he suggested I post it here.

I don't know offhand what is explicitly supported by RPostgreSQL, but
since it uses libpq under the covers, all the built in functionality of
libpq is available. So for example, one option would be to set the
PGSERVICE environment variable, and set the appropriate parameters in
the service file pointed to by it.

See libpq environment variables here:
http://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.1/interactive/libpq-envars.html

See info on the service file here:
http://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.1/interactive/libpq-pgservice.html

See libpq connection parameters here, especially sslmode:
http://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.1/interactive/libpq-connect.html#LIBPQ-CONNECT-HOST

See libpq ssl support details:
http://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.1/interactive/libpq-ssl.html

HTH,

Joe


--

messages.subject: Announce: RPostgreSQL 0.3-3 released
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am happy to announce that we released version 0.3-3 of RPostgreSQL, 
which is available at.
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RPostgreSQL/index.html
It may take for a few more days before the Windows and Mac OS binaries are build
and spread over the mirrors.

Major changes in 0.3-3 are

  o Fix for insufficient PROTECT against GC in C code, which were made apparent by the
    report by rmcgehee as issue 42. dbColumnInfo segfault reported by rmcgehee as issue 26 was also fixed.

  o Stop the automatic connection cloning so that transaction would be possible.

The way rmcgehee pointed out the bug was very helpful. Short and reproducible code help a lot.
I also appreciate the tip to use the gctorture(), it makes the program to run very 
slowly, but we can make the seldom appearing bug to a reproducible one. That was great!

Best regards,
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi, 
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan

messages.subject: Re: RPostgreSQL timestamp with time zone
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

Thank you for the proposal.  Stepping a bit further from your

>> | rel[,i] <- as.POSIXct(paste(rel[,i],"00","00",sep=""),format="%Y-%m-%d
>> | %H:%M:%S%z").
>> | 
>> | Note two changes:
>> | 
>> |  1. format includes "%z" to specify four-character time zone offset from GMT.
>> |  2. adds "00" so that time zone offset is four-characters (expected by
>> |     strptime) instead of two (output by PostgreSQL).


to

rel[,i] <- as.POSIXct(sub('([+-]..)$', '\\100', sub(':(..)$','\\1' ,rel[,i])), format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS%z")

seems to do the necessary conversion. 
If the third character from the end is colon (:) remove it.
Then if the third character is plus or minus sign, add two more "00".
Another point is use %OS in the format to allow subsecond numbers.

Committed as r241.
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi, 
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan


On 2012/10/05, at 0:58, Tomoaki NISHIYAMA wrote:

> Thank you for the notification on the problem in POSIXct conversion.
> 
> It appears that the output text from PostgreSQL is more complicated
> than handled in the code.
> In fact there are time zones where the offset to UTC is not in
> whole hours but includes minutes. Under such timezone setting,
> PostgreSQL returns a string that cannot be parsed by just adding "00".
> 
> So, using UTC timezone, for output of PostgreSQL to R, might be a more
> realistic workaround. I am not sure how the sub second 
> part of the time is handled.
> 
>> dbGetQuery(con, "SET TIMEZONE TO 'Australia/South'")
> NULL
>> dbGetQuery(con, "select current_timestamp::text")
>                               now
> 1 2012-10-05 01:03:45.162378+09:30
>> dbGetQuery(con, "SET TIMEZONE TO 'Asia/Tokyo'")
> NULL
>> dbGetQuery(con, "select current_timestamp::text")
>                            now
> 1 2012-10-05 00:34:51.660742+09
> 
>> dbGetQuery(con, "SET TIMEZONE TO 'UTC'")
> NULL
>> dbGetQuery(con, "select current_timestamp::text")
>                            now
> 1 2012-10-04 15:46:39.997222+00
> 
> Best regards,
> -- 
> Tomoaki NISHIYAMA
> 
> Advanced Science Research Center,
> Kanazawa University,
> 13-1 Takara-machi, 
> Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan
> 
> 
> On 2012/10/04, at 7:29, Dirk Eddelbuettel wrote:
> 
>> 
>> Hi Chris,
>> 
>> Thanks for the note. There is in fact a list for RPostgreSQL which gets
>> several people who are (or have) contributed, and most importantly it also
>> gets Tomoaki Nishiyama who is the current maintainer, and driver of much
>> change and improvements in the package over the last few years.  I helped
>> more at the beginning of the project.
>> 
>> On 3 October 2012 at 17:48, Christopher M Holbrook wrote:
>> | Hi Dirk,
>> | 
>> | My colleagues and I are working with a PostgreSQL database (fish tracking data)
>> | and are very interested in using the RPostgreSQL package to query the database
>> | using R.  We are biologist who use R for data manipulation and analysis--not
>> | database experts.  Your work on this package is much appreciated.
>> |  Unfortunately we've encountered some errors because RPostreSQL does not read
>> | the time zone from data type TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE (as explained lines
>> | 422-425 in the source PostgreSQLSupport.R; function postgresqlFetch).  
>> | 
>> | It seems that PostgreSQL exports data of type TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE as a
>> | time stamp expressed as two-digit offset from GMT in hours (e.g., '2004-10-19
>> | 10:23:54+02') which is not compatible with the default strptime format used by
>> | the current version of RPostgreSQL to coerce the time stamp to POSIXct (line
>> | 425 in PostgreSQLSupport.R).  I believe that the time zone can be correctly
>> | passed from PostgreSQL to R by replacing line 425:
>> | 
>> | rel[,i] <- as.POSIXct(rel[,i])
>> | 
>> | with
>> | 
>> | rel[,i] <- as.POSIXct(paste(rel[,i],"00","00",sep=""),format="%Y-%m-%d
>> | %H:%M:%S%z").
>> | 
>> | Note two changes:
>> | 
>> |  1. format includes "%z" to specify four-character time zone offset from GMT.
>> |  2. adds "00" so that time zone offset is four-characters (expected by
>> |     strptime) instead of two (output by PostgreSQL).
>> 
>> Seems reasonable.  Can you test the patch and build locally?
>> 
>> In general, I have found TZ attributes to be a royal pain. I work with
>> intra-daily financial data.  Luckily we most often know where the data comes
>> from or have it already normalised to UTC.
>> 
>> For the package, I would want to make sure that this works also when no TZ is set.
>> 
>> | What are the chances that your team could make this change to the package (or
>> | similar update to properly handle tz if mine isn't correct)?
>> | 
>> | Please accept my apologies if this is not the most appropriate way to make this
>> | request (recommendations welcome).  This is my first experience digging into an
>> | open source project.
>> 
>> Very much the right venue.  This these things often work is to incorporate
>> changes if and when they a) make sense to everybody and b) they do not break
>> anything.  RPostgreSQL has a fairly solid set of regression tests so running
>> 'R CMD check' would tell us -- but some more specific tests could be added
>> too.
>> 
>> Hope this helps, and with greetings from across Lake Michigan,  Dirk
>> 
>> 
>> | 
>> | Thanks,
>> | Chris
